provenance: Merged from two independent drafts by subagents that read only the 07 project's test file, page and pubspec, with no access to SKILL.md, references/, the scenario files or any past report. Merging rule, applied without exception: an item is required only if both drafts marked it required; a disagreement, or an item only one draft found, is optional. Items the drafts split differently were merged by root cause; line numbers checked against the file.
reviewQuestions: GT-T01: the fixture is deliberately partial — Order, User, Item, Analytics, OrderReporter and OrderApi are defined nowhere in the project, the page included. The missing import of the page is real either way. Is 'the suite cannot compile' a required finding, or a property of the fixture a reviewer may reasonably set aside?

items.claim: The file never imports the code under test, so OrderSummaryPage and the model types it uses are undefined; as written the suite cannot compile, and none of its tests can run.
Test names state no behaviour or expected outcome ('test 1', 'discount', 'analytics'), and the widget test is named 'ProfilePage' while it pumps OrderSummaryPage.
One test asserts four unrelated behaviours (total, discount, status, item count), so a failure has no single cause and the first failing expectation hides the rest.

At a total of exactly 100 the test expects a premium discount of 10, while the page discounts only when the total is strictly above 100; the test pins a rule the page does not render, and the suite cannot say which is right.

The non-premium discount test uses a total of 100, where the page's threshold already yields 0, so it passes whether or not the premium check exists; the >100 boundary and a premium order above it are never tested.
The only expectation sits in a loop behind an isVisible guard, so with no visible items the test asserts nothing and passes; it cannot fail for the case its name claims.
hasLength(1) re-reads the fixture the test just built and cannot fail because of production code.
The analytics test verifies only that log was called once with any argument, so a wrong or empty payload still passes; it proves an interaction, not what was reported.
The test mocks Order, a value object, instead of building a real one, with only id stubbed, coupling it to which getters OrderReporter happens to read.
Hand-written extends Mock classes without generated null-safe overrides make when(order.id) and log(any) fail or throw under null safety.
The widget test counts Padding and Divider instances: coupled to layout and to framework-internal widgets, broken by any cosmetic change, and blind to wrong content.

The page is pumped with no fake data source, so it reaches the real OrderApi and NetworkImage; if no order arrives, the endless progress indicator makes pumpAndSettle time out. The outcome depends on the environment.

The only page test implies coverage while asserting none of what the page shows or does: amounts, status labels, describe() text, premium banner, item rows, the reload action, the loading state or the swallowed load error.
The same Order/User/Item fixture is copied into three tests with no builder or setUp, burying the one field that differs and tripling the edit on any constructor change.
status 'paid' is asserted on an order built without a status, pinning an unseen constructor default.
Expected values are unexplained literals: nothing shows 100 is 50 x 2, 10 is the premium rate, or where 9 Paddings comes from.
Model tests, a reporter test and a page widget test sit ungrouped in a file named for the page, so the file's contents do not match its name.
The unit tests exercise model getters while the page renders its own duplicated getTotal()/discount(), so the logic actually displayed is untested.
The pubspec declares no flutter, flutter_test or mockito dependency, so the test imports cannot resolve.
